newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE steady in bullish sentiment, lack of factors.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE steady in bullish sentiment, lack of factors.

text.p: The benchmark three-month March euroyen futures contract was steady just below its contract high at midday on Friday amid a general lack of factors, although dealers reported bullish sentiment and said fresh highs could be possible next week.
But others said wariness about the contract's present strength could well lead to consolidation at current levels for some time.
The March ended the morning at 99.20, unchanged from Thursday's settlement and just below the contract high of 99.22 hit in Thursday morning trade. It moved from 99.18 to 99.20.

Sales by unspecified U.S. operators, probably funds, on SIMEX apparently pushed the March lower during early trade, but the firm sentiment inspired buying and helped erase these losses, one trust bank trader said.
"And we may see even more gains next week on spillover strength from Japanese government bonds (JGBs), which could take a shot at 127.00," he added.
But he also said, and others agreed, that the market appeared to be wary about taking March euroyen futures much higher at this point, and additional gains might be slow.

The next key point for the March is likely to be 99.25, with the downside solid near 99.15 over the next week. A trader with a city bank's securities arm said a decisive break above 99.23 could take the contract quickly up to 99.28.
The market will keep one eye on U.S. unemployment data, due out at 1230 GMT on Friday, to see how the U.S. bond market responds, but otherwise there are few new factors to be found.
Little impact is expected from Japan July domestic vehicle sales, due for release at 0500 GMT.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 400 billion into the money market in its regular morning operation.

Key overnight call money was being traded mainly at 0.50 percent, unchanged from Thursday's weighted average. Strong demand for short-term funds appeared to be keeping the overnight rate supported despite the generous operation, which kept the money market in surplus by around 300 billion yen.

Around 10 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.63 percent. On Thursday, around 10 billion yen of three-month CDs were issued at 0.63 percent and around 160 billion yen at 0.64 percent.
